title: Employee handbook: working at Redwood — overview, roles, benefits, hiring & tools
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview
========

This document is the canonical employee-facing summary for working at Redwood Inference. It consolidates the most-requested handbook topics: what to expect as a Redwood employee, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and a high-level guide to our primary internal tools and access procedures. This page is maintained by People Ops; please contact the page owner (people-ops@redwood.ai) for corrections.

1) Working at Redwood — quick summary
------------------------------------
- Mission alignment: We are a developer-first inference platform focused on production-grade LLM serving. Everyone is encouraged to tie work back to latency, reliability, cost, or developer experience.
- Culture highlights: mission-driven, asynchronous collaboration, high ownership, and bias toward shipping with strong QA.
- Hours & flexibility: Core overlap hours are 11:00–16:00 PT. We support distributed teams across NA, EU, and APAC; flexible remote-first policy with optional office days.
- Values: Customer empathy, technical excellence, operational reliability, and clear communication.

2) Roles and career ladders
---------------------------
Short overview: Redwood has clear IC and management ladders across Engineering, Product, Research, SRE, and Developer Experience. Ladders emphasize scope, impact, and mentorship. Promotions happen twice yearly (Spring/Fall) with ongoing calibration cycles.

Common role families and example levels (engineering-centric examples):

- Individual Contributor (IC) ladder:
  - E1 / Associate Engineer — early-career contributors; ownership of small features and bugs.
  - E2 / Engineer — delivers major features with guidance; contributes to design reviews.
  - E3 / Senior Engineer — owns cross-service features, mentors peers, leads code and design quality.
  - E4 / Staff Engineer — shapes architecture, leads multi-team initiatives, sets technical strategy.
  - E5 / Principal Engineer — company-level technical leadership, long-term platform vision, and outward-facing representation.

- Management ladder:
  - M1 / Engineering Manager — manages a small team (3–6), owns hiring and performance, and partners on roadmap.
  - M2 / Senior Manager — larger teams or multiple squads; drives cross-team execution and career development.
  - M3 / Director and above — org-level strategy, budget, and stakeholder relations.

Career cadence and expectations:
1. Goal-setting occurs quarterly using the Redwood goal template (see related_pages).
2. Performance reviews happen semi-annually; promotion packets should include impact statements, 360 feedback, and concrete metrics.
3. Mentorship & growth: employees are encouraged to have a skip-level mentor; manager and mentor responsibilities are tracked in workday.

Promotion checklist (IC example):
1. Articulate three measurable accomplishments in the review window.
2. Demonstrate consistent ownership across at least two cross-functional projects.
3. Exhibit mentorship by onboarding new hires or running learning sessions.
4. Provide architectural/design reviews with measurable quality improvements.

3) Benefits & perks — summary table
----------------------------------
Our benefits are designed to support health, financial security, learning, and family needs. Below is a high-level summary; the full benefits plan with provider links is in the benefits portal.

| Category | What you get | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Health & wellness | Medical (multiple plan tiers), dental, vision, HSA & FSA options | Coverage effective first day of month following 30 days of employment for most plans |
| Paid time off | 20 PTO days/year (prorated), 12 company holidays, 12 sick days | Additional parental leave (see below) |
| Parental leave | Primary caregiver: up to 18 weeks paid; Secondary caregiver: 8 weeks paid | Adoption and surrogacy supported; flexible return-to-work options |
| Financial | Competitive base + equity package; 401(k) with company match (US) | Equity grants follow role and seniority; RSU schedule in offer letter |
| Learning & development | $2,000 annual L&D stipend; 5 paid conference days | Manager approval required for external paid courses >$500 |
| Perks | Commuter stipend (region-dependent), wellness stipend, home office setup allowance | Regular team events and virtual social stipends |

How to use benefits:
- Enroll within 30 days of eligibility via the HR portal.
- For parental leave, submit the request to People Ops at least 30 days before expected leave when feasible.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview
--------------------------------
Hiring principles:
- Structured interviews: role-specific rubric, take-home exercises only when necessary, clear evaluation criteria.
- Inclusive hiring: diverse slate, interview training for all interviewers, and consistent debriefs.
- Time-to-offer target: 2–3 weeks from first interview to offer for most IC roles; extended roles (executive, legal-sensitive) may take longer.

Standard interview loop (software engineering example):
1. Recruiter screen (30–45 min) — culture fit, high-level experience.
2. Technical screen (45–60 min) — coding or system-design depending on level.
3. Onsite / virtual loop (3–5 interviews) — product/system design, coding, behavioral, and cross-functional partner interviews.
4. Debrief and calibration — hiring manager + panel reach decision within 48 hours of last interview.
5. Offer & negotiation — People Ops and hiring manager finalize compensation; target accept within 7 days.

New hire onboarding (first 90 days):
- Pre-boarding (before start): IT asset order, Okta/SSO invite, benefits forms, and first-week schedule.
- Day 1: Welcome orientation, team intro, security training, and first 1:1 with manager.
- Week 1: Buddy program meeting, product overview sessions, and initial tickets/tasks assigned.
- Month 1: First deliverable, triage 1:1 cadence with manager weekly.
- Month 3: 90-day review with manager to confirm ramp and goals.

Essential onboarding checklist (new hire to-dos):
1. Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment.
2. Finish security and privacy training modules.
3. Get access to GitHub org, primary repos, CI/CD, and cloud accounts.
4. Join team Slack channels and calendar groups.
5. Schedule skip-level intro and cross-functional meet-and-greets.

Manager onboarding responsibilities (first 30 days):
1. Prepare a 30/60/90 plan for the hire.
2. Assign a buddy and set weekly 1:1s.
3. Ensure required infra and tools access is provisioned.
4. Add the hire to team project boards and relevant dashboards.

5) Internal tools guide — quick reference
--------------------------------------
This section lists the primary internal tools, their purpose, and first-access steps. For tool-specific walkthroughs and screenshots, see the eng-developer-experience Quickstarts.

- Slack (communication)
  - Purpose: day-to-day team communication, alerts, incident channels.
  - Access: Provisioned via Okta SSO. Join #announcements, #engineering, and your team channel.
  - Etiquette: use threads, set DO NOT DISTURB during focus blocks, and @mention only when necessary.

- Okta & SSO (identity)
  - Purpose: Single sign-on for most corporate apps (Confluence, GitHub, GCP/AWS accounts, 1Password).
  - Access: People Ops creates Okta account during pre-boarding. For access issues open a ticket to IT.

- Confluence (documentation)
  - Purpose: company docs, runbooks, playbooks, and product specs.
  - Tip: write docs as polished references; use templates in the company-handbook space.

- GitHub (code host)
  - Purpose: source control and PR-based development.
  - Access: request via the Access Request workflow in the IT portal; approvals from repo owner and manager required.
  - Important repos: inference-runtime, infra, redwood-sdk, internal-evals.

- JIRA (task tracking)
  - Purpose: sprint planning, bugs, and cross-team dependencies.
  - Access: Okta provisioned; join your team board and weekly standups. Use labels: team:, product:, priority:.

- CI/CD & deployment consoles
  - Purpose: build pipelines, canary rollouts, and deployment dashboards.
  - Access: team infra leads grant environment-specific rights; follow the deployment runbook for production changes.

- 1Password (secrets)
  - Purpose: team vaults for credentials and API keys.
  - Access: provisioned via Okta. Never store secrets in docs or code.

- Internal analytics & dashboards (observability)
  - Purpose: latency and cost dashboards, model performance, error rates.
  - Access: request through eng-platform dashboards-and-alerts; include justification and owners.

Access request & escalation procedure
- Initial access: Most tools are auto-provisioned via Okta within 24–48 hours of start date once the IT request is submitted.
- If access is delayed beyond 72 hours: open an IT ticket and CC your manager + People Ops.
- For production access (secrets, infra prod accounts): require manager approval and completion of production access checklist (training + attestation).

6) Practical policies and useful links
------------------------------------
- PTO approval: submit requests in Workday at least 5 business days in advance for planned time off. For extended time off (>2 weeks) notify People Ops.
- Expense policy: receipts required for reimbursements >$25; standard per-diem rules apply for travel.
- Incident participation: all on-call engineers follow the oncall-and-incident-response runbooks; incident follow-ups go to the incident-review board.

Useful links (internal):
- Benefits portal: /benefits/portal
- Onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-checklist
- Promotion & performance templates: /confluence/company-handbook/performance-templates
- IT access request form: /internal/it/access-request
- Eng quickstarts & SDKs: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates

7) Ownership and maintenance
----------------------------
- Document owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Review cadence: This page is reviewed quarterly; People Ops will solicit updates from Eng, Product, and Security teams before each review.
- How to propose changes: Use the Confluence edit UI and request People Ops as a reviewer. For major policy changes (benefits, parental leave, time-off) notify HR leadership and Legal.

Appendix A — Sample 30/60/90 plan (text)
--------------------------------------
30 days:
- Complete security and product orientation.
- Deliver first small ticket or documentation update.
- Attend product and architecture overview sessions.

60 days:
- Lead a small project or feature area.
- Present findings from a codebase deep-dive.
- Mentor a newer teammate.

90 days:
- Ship a measurable impact (bugfix, feature, or performance work) and present results.
- 90-day review with manager to confirm goals and next steps.

End of document.
